_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY — placeholders. Copy to secrets.<env>.json (git-ignored), fill real values there. Never commit real secrets. See README.md → 'Environments' and 'Secrets to replace for production'.
_comment_environment: 'environment' is LOAD-BEARING: it yields the env code (development->dev, production->prod) that prefixes every project-global GCP id and names the per-environment state bucket. Teardown destroys the WORKLOAD layer only for EVERY environment (the DNS zone + state bucket are always preserved — they cost almost nothing to keep); a non-production 'teardown --purge' ALSO destroys the DNS zone + state bucket + sweeps secrets (production forbids --purge). Run 'spacestroker-deploy validate' to see every derived id.
_comment_monitoring: MONITORING (production only): the dashboard, uptime checks and Cloud Armor log-based metrics are created whenever 'environment' is production -- there is no toggle to set, the deploy tool derives it. The BUDGET additionally needs billingAccountId + alertEmail; leave either empty and the budget and its notification channel are simply SKIPPED (the apply still succeeds). A budget is created against the BILLING ACCOUNT, which sits ABOVE the project, so the deploying principal also needs roles/billing.costsManager granted THERE -- no project-level role provides it. Both fields are plain config rather than credentials, but never commit real values. Enable the two APIs first: gcloud services enable monitoring.googleapis.com billingbudgets.googleapis.com
_comment_orbit: ORBIT (#121/#122/#123) — three secrets, and PRODUCTION MUST SET ALL THREE. The custody keypair is SEPARATE from the payout keypair on purpose: sharing them makes 'player balances vs on-chain balance' uncheckable and turns an Orbit stake into a same-account no-op transfer. ⚠️ Committed config ships a REAL devnet Orbit keypair so the local stack works out of the box, so an environment that omits PublicKey/PrivateKey boots with Orbit ENABLED against devnet instead of failing closed — override both explicitly. The session secret signs the ~7-day read tokens; rotating it signs everyone out (contained: one signature recovers). The Telegram bot token sits in the PATH of every Bot API call, which is why the whole URL is treated as a secret and never logged; leave it OUT (or blank) and Telegram is simply INERT — no calls, and the modal hides the section.
_comment_clusterUrl: GeneralSettings:Token:ClusterUrl is a SECRET, not appConfig: the RPC provider's api-key rides in the URL's query string, and appConfig entries become plaintext Cloud Run env vars. Devnet form: https://devnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=... The FALLBACK below is a plain public endpoint with no key, so it stays in appConfig.
_comment_houseSeed: House seed bet (#168), PRODUCTION-ONLY: the house wallet places one ordinary paid stake into every newly opened round, so a round is never empty and a single real player can start it. BOTH halves are required and a MOCK_ value counts as ABSENT (HouseSeedSettings.IsConfigured is fail-CLOSED), so a half-filled block silently disables seeding instead of erroring — and the 'not configured' line logs at Information, which Production's Warning floor drops. It MUST be a separate keypair from TokenOwner* (identical sender and recipient makes the SPL transfer a 0-delta no-op that is then refused as underpaid, AFTER it confirms) and from Orbit (that is player CUSTODY money).
_comment_analytics: GA4: ONE measurement id serves BOTH properties — the app reads VUE_APP_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and the landing page reads PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID, so set them to the SAME G-XXXXXXXXXX. That is what keeps the LP -> app hop a single session (same registrable domain, shared _ga cookie), so a bet is attributed to the campaign that brought the visitor. Both live in frontBuild because the deploy tool writes that same block into BOTH repo builds and each toolchain only exposes its own prefix (Vue CLI: VUE_APP_*, Astro/Vite: PUBLIC_*). EMPTY = analytics never loads: no script, no cookie, no consent banner — keep them empty in secrets.development.json so dev never reports into the production property. The id is public in the page source, so it is config rather than a credential, but still never commit a real one.
_comment_orbit_flag: ORBIT FRONTEND GATE (#146): VUE_APP_ORBIT_ENABLED in frontBuild decides whether the SPA SHOWS Orbit; the three Orbit secrets above decide whether the BACKEND engine is configured. They are independent — the engine keeps running on a flag-off build, which is safe only while no player is enrolled and no game type has AllowOrbit=true (verify that once against production before deploying with the flag off). FAIL-CLOSED: only the exact string 'true' enables it, so omitting the key ships Orbit hidden. production: 'false' (not production-deliverable yet); development: 'true'.
_comment_token_mint: TOKEN LAUNCH (#160): ONE value — the SPL MINT ADDRESS of the launched pump.fun token — serves BOTH builds. The app reads VUE_APP_TOKEN_MINT and the landing page reads PUBLIC_TOKEN_MINT, so set them to the SAME address; both live in frontBuild because the deploy tool writes that block into both repo builds and each toolchain only exposes its own prefix. EMPTY = the PRE-LAUNCH state on both sites: the LP keeps its 'No token. Yet.' panel with the anti-scam warning, and the app renders no token card and no header token button. FAIL-CLOSED — anything that is not a plausible base58 mint is treated as empty, so a Buy button can never point at nothing. WARNING: THIS IS NOT VUE_APP_GAME_TOKEN_ADDRESS. That is the SETTLEMENT mint the games actually pay out in; the two are independent, and conflating them means changing one silently changes the other. Rounds settle in USDC and this token is information only. WARNING: both sites are STATIC builds, so filling this in is a REBUILD + REDEPLOY OF TWO SITES, not a runtime toggle — launch day must deploy both or they disagree. The mint is public information rather than a credential, but keep it empty here and in development; the real value belongs in secrets.production.json.
_comment_treasury_wallet: TOKEN LAUNCH (#160): the address holding the game treasury. ONE value, BOTH builds — the landing page reads PUBLIC_TREASURY_WALLET and the app reads VUE_APP_TREASURY_WALLET, so set them to the SAME address. Two sites publishing two different treasuries is worse than neither publishing one. Rendered on both as a copyable bar with a Solscan link: on the LP inside its treasury block, in the app inside the /how-to-play token section (the app stopped pointing at the landing page for this on 2026-08-12 — the manual is the surface that states the real figures). EMPTY = that address bar is simply not rendered on either site; the rest of the treasury block (the supply chart and the legend) still shows, because the split is content and lives in each repo's constants file, not here. FAIL-CLOSED — anything that is not a plausible base58 address is treated as empty, so neither site can ever publish a truncated or half-typed wallet. Independent of the mint: a build may legitimately have a live mint and no wallet configured. This is a PUBLIC address, never a private key: the treasury's key material must never appear in this file or any other. Like the mint, it is baked into static builds, so filling it in is a rebuild + redeploy of BOTH sites.
